clue.text: Such a letdown, losing bishop for pawn? Feeble!

indicators.note: the word for a letdown gives up one of its letters, which is swapped out
says which chess piece comes in to take the departing one's place

parts.note: bathetic describes an anticlimax, a sudden drop from the lofty to the trivial
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player bemoans a feeble exchange: giving up a bishop for a mere pawn is such a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing ... for' swaps the B of BATHETIC for a P.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean weak or pitifully inadequate, a common synonym pairing.

clue.text: Potentially future tree has a hard growth

parts.note: a corn is a hard thickening of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: An oak in the making sprouts a tough knobbly growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak's nut, planted, may grow into a tree: a tree in potential.

clue.text: Demonstrably zealous, slightly drunk and a bit diseased?

parts.note: happy is a jokey word for tipsy
the clap is slang for gonorrhoea, so clappy jocularly means having it

explanation.surface: Someone over-enthusiastic is tipsy and perhaps a little unwell too.
explanation.walkthrough: HAPPY-CLAPPY is a British informal, mildly mocking term for evangelical Christians who worship with exuberant clapping and singing.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes worshippers whose religious fervour is loudly and outwardly displayed.

clue.text: Resolve to set up free of tax at Geneva, for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: net income is what is left after tax
A as a short form of at, seen in prices like 3 apples a pound
Geneva is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A decision to establish a tax haven in Swiss Geneva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns NET into TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun is firmness of purpose, the same as doggedness.

clue.text: Showing backbone, join chorus of disapproval about almost cheeky message being garbled

parts.note: a chine is an animal's spine, or a cut of meat including it
to sew is to join with stitches

indicators.note: the boos go around the next piece

parts.note: an audience hiss shows collective disapproval

indicators.note: the word for cheeky is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: pert means impudent or saucy

explanation.surface: A spirited person joins in booing a saucy message that has been scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the word for cheeky, and 'about' wraps the boos round it. 'Showing' is a link word; chine is a butcher's word for the backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the party game in which a whispered phrase is passed along and becomes distorted.

clue.text: Bad air is little by little infecting mother

indicators.note: the two letters of the word 'is' go in one at a time, at separate places, not as a pair
getting inside, as an infection does, so letters go within the word for mother

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
the word is supplies both letters, put in separately
the word is supplies both letters, put in separately

explanation.surface: Polluted air is gradually making a mother ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' goes into MAMA in two separate pieces ('little by little infecting'): I after the first M, S after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy vapour, once thought to spread disease.

clue.text: Grumble quietly and interminably about a change

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the next letter
without its end, so the last letter of the grumbling word goes

parts.note: to mutter is to complain under one's breath

explanation.surface: Someone moans softly and endlessly about some alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' trims MUTTER to MUTTE, which goes 'about' A.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form or nature.

clue.text: In town, pay rent, but not in full

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the town is a fragment of them

explanation.surface: Living in a town, someone pays only part of their rent.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a Scottish seaside town, county town of Ayrshire.

clue.text: As war leader, in short time I sort of turn defeat on its head

indicators.note: the turn and the overturned defeat sit inside the short time

parts.note: min is the abbreviation for minute
a U-turn, so U

indicators.note: turned upside down, in a down clue the word for defeat is read bottom to top

parts.note: a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A wartime leader quickly reverses a defeat into success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on its head' turns the word for defeat backwards, as befits a down clue. Mussolini was Italy's Fascist dictator in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini led Italy into the Second World War, an example of a wartime leader.

clue.text: Great achievement, working ticket

parts.note: a coup is a notable success
on, as in a machine switched on and running

explanation.surface: Getting a working ticket is quite an accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher or ticket exchanged for goods or a discount.

clue.text: Hobby horse taken out from among the others

parts.note: in, as in among the crowd

indicators.note: a letter is removed from the combined words

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A favourite horse is withdrawn from a field of runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out from' removes H from INTHEREST. 'Hobby horse' looks like one phrase, but 'Hobby' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a pastime one pursues for pleasure.

clue.text: Such a child follows if expressing hopeless wish

definitions.meaning: a child with no brothers or sisters
the word placed after 'if' in a wish that cannot come true

explanation.definitionFit: It names a child without siblings, and completes the wistful phrase of longing for the impossible.

clue.text: Writer using part of body toner, exercising

parts.note: the chest is part of the torso

indicators.note: working out puts the following word's letters through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: An author uses a body-toning product while working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges TONER into TERTON. G. K. Chesterton was an English writer, creator of Father Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English novelist, essayist and poet.

clue.text: One investor is frightful heretic

indicators.note: awful, so the letters are thrown into a dreadful jumble

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor who is a terrible dissenter from orthodoxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges I with INVESTOR and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A revisionist departs from established doctrine, as a heretic does from accepted belief.

clue.text: Simple meal as husband's away from home, one posted briefly

indicators.note: one letter is absent from the word for home

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: cut short, the last letter of the posted item goes

parts.note: a letter is something sent by post

explanation.surface: A quick supper while a husband is away, eaten after he has written home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' drops H from HOME; 'briefly' cuts LETTER to LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs cooked in a pan make an easy, basic dish.

clue.text: Priest finally constrained by ethical principles — it's the human condition

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the word for ethical principles

parts.note: morality is a set of principles of right conduct

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Priest is used

explanation.surface: A priest is ultimately bound by a moral code, a part of being human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T, which 'constrained by' places inside MORALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being subject to death is the defining fate of all people.

clue.text: Worthless article found in Bordeaux?

indicators.note: the article sits inside the word for wine

parts.note: Bordeaux is a French wine, and vin is French for wine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A worthless item discovered in the French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux?' with its question mark points to a French word: VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain can mean futile or of no value, as in a vain attempt.

clue.text: Quietly rubbish old army officer etiquette

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
rot means nonsense
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A colonel softly dismisses old-fashioned manners as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal code of correct conduct on official occasions.

clue.text: Graze stock

definitions.meaning: animals grazing bite off the tops of plants
the stock of a whip is its handle

explanation.definitionFit: To crop is to eat grass short; a crop is also the handle or stock of a whip.

clue.text: Poverty daughter's in severe, with very little money

indicators.note: the daughter goes inside the word for severe

parts.note: harsh means severe
D is the abbreviation for daughter, the 's standing for is
1p, one penny, written as IP

explanation.surface: A daughter lives in harsh poverty with hardly any cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 1p (one penny) is read as IP, the digit 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship means suffering through want, especially lack of money.

clue.text: Botched delivery drama: born at a couple of pounds

parts.note: Noh is a Japanese drama form, also spelt No
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them

explanation.surface: A dramatic premature birth of a baby weighing only two pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A NO BALL in cricket is an illegal delivery by the bowler, penalised with a run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an illegally bowled ball is called this, so it is a faulty delivery.

clue.text: Gently play with seaside toy

indicators.note: toying with the letters reorders them

explanation.surface: Be careful handling the children's beach toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play with' rearranges SEASIDETOY.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhortation to proceed carefully and without haste.

clue.text: One in a ring perhaps, but friendless?

parts.note: nought pal, zero friends, is read as O and PAL

explanation.surface: A gemstone in a ring, yet lonely.
explanation.walkthrough: Being friendless is having a pal count of O (nought).
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone is often set in rings, as an example.

clue.text: Hate one endlessly tedious, but hard to interrupt

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the shortened word
missing its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bore is someone tedious
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A boring person's endless chatter is interrupted, but he is hard to hate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BORE to BOR; 'to interrupt' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe.

clue.text: Foremost of mandarins, I will compete in the fast stream

indicators.note: the leading letter of mandarins

parts.note: contracted to I'll
to race is to compete

explanation.surface: The top civil servant declares they will compete in the fast track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foremost of' gives M. Mandarins are senior civil servants, and the fast stream is the UK civil service graduate scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the swift channel of water that drives a mill wheel.

clue.text: Throw up lunch over barmaid — just the starters

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the three words are used

explanation.surface: Being sick over the barmaid after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just the starters' takes L, O, B.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to toss something high into the air.

clue.text: Elegant greeting is pretentious

parts.note: chic means stylish
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: A stylish hello is showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi means affectedly fussy or showy.

clue.text: One clashed as representative's spoken

indicators.note: said out loud, the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a symbol represents something else

explanation.surface: Someone clashed with a delegate over what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One clashed' looks like a person in a quarrel; it is a percussion instrument struck against another.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbals are brass plates struck together, so each is something clashed.

clue.text: Very bookish — unhesitatingly — and friendless

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: without er, the sound of hesitation, so those two letters go

parts.note: literary means fond of books

explanation.surface: A very bookish person, quick to speak, yet without friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhesitatingly' removes ER from LITERARY, leaving LITARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary means alone, without companions.
